## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `d319685aa5739f11b7f7330d687e790a02d5b79d`
Local-runs: probe — one substring check of the eval cases at the head against their own assertions (S1); nothing built, run or re-run
Scope: skills/objectstack-formula/SKILL.md, skills/objectstack-formula/evals/cel-predicates-formulas.json + none
Security-touching: yes

Read: card #36217 (body and all four comments), PR #36354 (body, file list, net diff against merge-base `b3bcfefcb`), the 54 check-runs on the head, and the cited code on `origin/main` `9abc7321` (`packages/formula/src/validate.ts`, `packages/formula/src/cel-to-filter.ts`, `packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.ts`, `packages/lint/src/validate-sharing-rule-enforceability.ts`, `packages/qa/scenarios/src/skill-evals/grade.ts`, `packages/spec/src/data/field-value.zod.ts`). The diff holds no file that implements or enforces the two `hits` files, so the scope adds none; the changeset is the lane seat's.

Why `Security-touching: yes`: the new note is an unqualified rule for every CEL surface the skill lists, and that table lists `SharingRule` `condition`. At that surface the form the note marks RIGHT produces a sharing rule that grants nothing (M1). The teaching reaches sharing behaviour although the path and the hunk do not name it, and the fix will have to teach the sharing-rule spelling.

### ① Derived judgments

- Check-runs on the head: every completed run is `success` or `skipped`, none failed or pending. Among them Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · CI, release & engine gates, the Type Check family, Build Core and Test Core. Right: the derived gate families are answered by CI.
- Accept-set: no schema, validator or runtime code changes. No authored input is newly accepted or refused. Right.
- Public surface: the published `objectstack-formula` skill gains one note and loses six restatements; the eval file gains case 13. Right as a description of what ships.
- The six deletions, each checked against the file at the head: every cut statement still has a home (cheat-sheet row `Key existence (NOT null-safety)` and the WRONG block comment; `Verify your work`; the `previous` table's first row; that table's `after*` row; "the platform refuses" in the same paragraph; the cheat-sheet `String literal` row). Right: no teaching is lost.
- Token ceiling: unchanged at 6008, the ratchet gate is green in CI. Right.
- The head is behind `main`: PR #36340 (`cb5a9755`, the per-site list-equality rewrite) merged after this branch's merge-base and before this review. No file of this diff conflicts, but the validator text the note mirrors has changed. Wrong as it stands: see M1.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/36217-formula-skill-list-equality.md` is a `patch` for `@objectstack/skills`, the package that ships `skills/**`. A wording-only skill change with one added eval case publishes nothing above patch. The level is right.

Clause-②: no — correct: the diff refuses no input and narrows no declared capability; it documents a refusal `@objectstack/formula` already ships. `Metadata-protocol: none` is correct as well. The changeset's prose names "the two forms that replace it"; it must follow whatever M1's fix teaches.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Deviation, six same-file cuts outside the claim's operator-table area: accepted. Same file, no restructuring, each home verified in ①.
- Deviation, guarded forms taught where the card names bare forms: the direction is right (`'a' in null` faults, as `checkListEquality`'s own doc says), but the spelling is the one from before PR #36340. See M1.
- Open question, "should this follow-up carry an eval case": answered B by commit `d319685a`, which adds case 13. The case itself is defective: see S1.
- Card comment 7076555075 (seat 7 pointer: teach the per-site spellings of PR #36340, namely `has()`-guarded reads, `.contains()` at sharing-rule conditions, parenthesised comparisons): NOT answered by this head. PR #36340's own body carries `Skills-docs: follow-up #36217`, so this card is the named carrier of that teaching. See M1.
- Out-of-scope finding (bare forms validate yet fault on `null`): noted, no action owed; the validator's refusal prescribes a guarded form.
- SQL push-down: no code in the diff, so no id materialisation and no in-app join. One push-down fact does bear on the text: the taught `in` form does not lower to a query filter at the one surface that compiles to SQL (M1).

### ④ Design judgment

**`skills/objectstack-formula/SKILL.md`**

M1 (must-fix) — the note marks `record.tags != null && 'vip' in record.tags` (and its `.exists()` and `!=` variants) as RIGHT with no site qualifier, and on `main` that form is wrong at a surface the same skill lists as CEL. `SharingRule` `condition` is in the skill's "CEL surfaces" table. A sharing-rule condition is never evaluated as CEL: it is compiled by `compileCelToFilter`, and `lowerMembership` (`packages/formula/src/cel-to-filter.ts:389-393`) throws "`in` requires a field on the left (got literal)". `packages/formula/src/validate-list-equality-36167.test.ts:370-373` pins exactly this: `compileCelToFilter('record.f != null && "a" in record.f')` answers `ok: false`. The consequence is in `packages/lint/src/validate-sharing-rule-enforceability.ts`: the build reports an unlowerable-condition error, and at runtime the rule is skipped and grants nothing. So an agent that follows the note at a sharing rule writes a condition that is refused, on the very field type the note is about, which is the failure the card exists to remove. Since PR #36340 the validator prescribes three spellings (`listMembershipRewrite`, `packages/formula/src/validate.ts:1629-1650`): `(has(record.f) && record.f != null && "v" in record.f)` for a `record.` / `previous.` read evaluated as CEL, `(f != null && "v" in f)` for a bare name at a flow condition, and `(record.f != null && record.f.contains("v"))` where the source compiles to a filter. The note teaches none of the three as the validator writes it, and the third not at all. Fix: rebase on `main` and teach the per-site spelling, at minimum `.contains()` for a sharing-rule `condition`, and say that the `in` form is for conditions evaluated as CEL. The `has()` guard at action `visible` / `disabled` is already covered by the skill's own "client-side and sparse" paragraph, so a pointer to it is enough there. Keep the rewrite parenthesised or say so: `A && record.tags == null || !('vip' in record.tags)` does not mean what the unparenthesised `!=` line suggests. The token ceiling has 1 token of headroom, so this needs further same-file deletion or a ruling on the ceiling.

N1 (nit) — the list of list-valued fields is not the full set. `MULTI_CAPABLE_TYPES` (`packages/spec/src/data/field-value.zod.ts:365-367`) is `select`, `radio`, `lookup`, `user`, `file`, `image`; the note names three. Also, the refusal fires only against a scalar literal (`scalarLiteralOf`), and at a flow condition only where the run binds the typed row; "a scalar" is slightly wider than the code. Neither misleads an author into a wrong expression.

The rest of the note holds against the code: the code `list-equality` and the opening words "list compared with a scalar" match `listEqualityRefusal`; `multiselect` / `checkboxes` / `tags` is `MULTI_OPTION_TYPES` exactly; "one constant on every row" is the validator's own reason; the taught forms are correct at every server-evaluated CEL site, where the skill's `has()` section already says `record` is total and `!= null` is the whole guard.

**`skills/objectstack-formula/evals/cel-predicates-formulas.json`**

S1 (should-fix) — case 13's reference answer fails case 13's own assertions. `must_not_contain` holds `record.labels == 'urgent'`, and `expected_output` contains that exact string, where it names the refused form. The grader (`packages/qa/scenarios/src/skill-evals/grade.ts`) matches a literal, case-sensitive substring with no normalisation, so the reference answer is graded FAIL. Cases 1 to 12 are all self-consistent on the same check; 13 is the only one that is not. This is the defect class `.changeset/35095-eval-forbidden-mention.md` removed from sixteen cases: a forbidden token that also fails a correct answer naming it as the thing to avoid. It is worse here because the skill note itself shows the refused line beside the right one, so a with-skill answer that mirrors the skill is the one most likely to be failed. Second, smaller arm of the same finding: the note offers `record.tags.exists(t, t == 'vip')` as RIGHT, and an answer in that form lacks the required `in record.labels` and fails too. Fix: forbid a spelling only a wrong answer writes (for example the whole wrong literal, `` P`record.labels == 'urgent'` ``) or drop the entry and rely on `must_contain`; and either accept the `.exists()` form or stop offering it in the note.

The prompt itself is a fair scenario for the card: a hook `condition` over a `tags` field is a server-evaluated site where `record` is total, so `record.labels != null && 'urgent' in record.labels` is correct there, and an answer in the validator's current `has()`-guarded spelling also satisfies both `must_contain` tokens.

Open on this head: M1, S1. N1 may be folded into the M1 fix or left.

## 维护者速读（席位记录 · head `5dfda71519`）

- 改了什么：对外发布的公式技能里加了一段说明。多值字段（标签、多选这类）不能直接和单个值比相等。说明按条件所在的位置给出对应的正确写法：普通条件、流程条件、共享规则条件各一种，并为此删掉了同一文件里六处重复说法，没有超过字数上限。另外加了两道技能自测题。
- 为什么：校验器已经拒绝这种比较，但技能没教该怎么改。尤其是共享规则，照普通写法写的条件在构建时会被拒，规则不生效。
- 风险：只改技能文字、两道自测题和发布说明，没有改代码。
- 要你做什么：批准这个受治理的技能改动。契约审核结论：通过，评论 7081992501，`Head-sha` 5dfda715190af861e741ef5b76ab8e8639ebd9a5。
- 席位意见：建议批准。
